title: Appalachian cryptids to be topic of Lindsey Wilson University talk
excerpt: Creatures said to roam the woods and haunt the night will be the subject of the next “SnackChat” at Lindsey Wilson University.
content:
COLUMBIA, Ky. (WDRB+WAVE) — Mothman. Bigfoot. Creatures said to roam the woods and haunt the night will be the subject of the next “SnackChat” at Lindsey Wilson University, just in time for Halloween

English professor Harold Bosstick will discuss Appalachian cryptids at 2 p.m. CT Wednesday, Oct. 21, in the Thomas D. Clark Reading Room at the Katie Murrell A. Library. The event is free and open to the public, with light snacks and refreshments.

Cryptids are creatures people believe exist, though their existence has not been scientifically proven or documented. Well-known examples include Bigfoot, which has reportedly been sighted in south-central Kentucky; the Kentucky Dogman, also known as the Beast of the Land Between the Lakes; and the Pope Lick Monster, also known as the Louisville Goatman.

Bosstick’s presentation will focus on lesser-known cryptids, including West Virginia’s Flatwoods humanoid, the “goblins” reported in the 1955 Hopkinsville encounter—also known as the Kelly Green Men Case—and the squonk, a creature from Pennsylvania’s Pocono Mountains.

Bosstick studied folklore while earning his doctorate in English, drawing on a lifelong interest in monsters and extraterrestrial creatures that began with the 1990s science-fiction series “The X-Files.”

Whether the creatures are real may be beside the point, Bosstick said. Stories about them can reveal something about the culture and way of life of the people who tell them.
